query: A Guest Who Offers Patronage {An old collector of books has asked for "the student who reads". He wants company and argument, and he says he funds promising young minds.|The old collector is back with a new pile of books and a new argument. He has been thinking about what you said, for a month.|The collector again. He calls you his protégé to the whole room now, which is flattering and a little alarming.} Take the patron's purse {He funds your books for the term, and wants you at his table every week. You argue till two, and sleep through a lecture.|The purse is generous and so is the argument, which runs until the candles do. Your coursework waits.|He pays you to disagree with him. You are good at it, and your exam reading is not getting done.} Ask to borrow his books {He beams, and lends you three books older than the castle. You read them on the walk home by moonlight.|He lends you his annotated copy, full of furious notes in the margin. They are better than the book.|"Finally," he says, "someone who wants the books more than the money." He gives you a small purse anyway.}
